events.title: U.S. Factory Orders Jump More Than Expected In September
events.description: The Commerce Department released a report on Tuesday showing new orders for U.S. manufactured goods surged by more than expected in the month of September. The report said factory orders shot up by 1.8 percent in September after rising by an upwardly revised 0.3 percent in August. Economists had expected factory orders to jump by 1.2 percent.

events.title: U.S. Job Openings Increase More Than Expected In September
events.description: A report released by the Labor Department on Tuesday showed a bigger-than-expected increase in job openings in the U.S. in the month of September. The Labor Department said job openings climbed to 7.523 million in September from an upwardly revised 7.190 million in August.

events.title: FTSE 100 Trades Lower
events.description: The FTSE 100 benchmark of the London Stock Exchange declined on Tuesday as global markets geared for the outcome of the U.S. midterm election results. The decline in crude oil prices that followed comments by U.S. President Donald Trump about ending financial support for Israel was also reflected in stock prices.

events.title: CAC 40 Weak Amidst Tech Fears
events.description: The CAC 40 index that tracks the 40 largest French stocks based on the Euronext Paris slipped on Tuesday as markets focused on the U.S. midterm elections as well as the latest margin warning by tech giant Apple.

events.title: DAX Slips On Tuesday
events.description: The DAX benchmark that tracks the performance of the 40 largest companies listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange declined on Tuesday as worries about the outcome of U.S. elections, lingering fears about elevated AI valuations, and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East dampened sentiment.

events.title: Canadian Dollar Rises As Oil Prices Rebound
events.description: The Canadian dollar strengthened against other major currencies in the European session on Tuesday, as the crude oil prices rebounded after a reported U.S. attack on Qeshm Island on the eve of crucial midterm elections.

events.title: Canadian Dollar Rises Against Majors
events.description: The Canadian dollar strengthened against other major currencies in the European session on Tuesday.

events.title: Indian Shares Extend Gains For Fourth Day
events.description: Indian shares closed Tuesday's session on a buoyant note, extending gains for a fourth consecutive session after Brent crude futures slumped nearly 8 percent on Monday amid signs of diplomatic progress between the U.S. and Iran.

events.title: Gold Edges Lower As Americans Vote In Midterms
events.description: Gold prices fell toward $3,900 an ounce on Tuesday after the United States reportedly struck Iran's strategic Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, the latest in a series of limited strikes on the country in recent weeks.

events.title: Australia Hikes Key Rate To 4.85%; Highest Since 2008
events.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its benchmark interest rate for the fifth time this year to the highest level in 18 years in order to bring inflation sustainably back to the target. The board, governed by Michele Bullock, voted 6-3 to lift the cash rate target by 25 basis points to 4.85 percent, marking the highest rate since 2008.

events.title: Oil Prices Rebound As US Strikes Iran's Qeshm Island
events.description: Oil prices rebounded on Tuesday after a reported U.S. attack on Qeshm Island on the eve of crucial midterm elections.

events.title: European Shares Retreat Amid Tech Selloff
events.description: European stocks edged lower on Tuesday as Apple delivered a mixed earnings report and oil prices rebounded to around $107 a barrel after a reported U.S. attack on Qeshm Island on the eve of crucial midterm elections.

events.title: Antipodean Currencies Fall Amid Risk-Off Mood
events.description: The antipodean currencies such as the Australia and the New Zealand dollars weakened against their major currencies in the Asian session on Tuesday, as Asian stock markets traded lower as South Korean markets tumbled amid weakness in semiconductor stocks on concerns over returns on huge AI spending and mixed earnings and cautious forecasts from major US technology firms.
